Article Title: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian, who famously warned internet has become ‘less human’, now says AI ‘can cause a lot of harm’
Article Text:
Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian

The age of 'AI Slop' and dead internet

Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian believes the internet as we know it is fundamentally broken, and artificial intelligence (AI) is both a symptom and a driver of the shift. Speaking with WIRED at the inaugural WIRED World Fair recently, Ohanian warned that while AI holds massive promise, “there is still a very real chance that this technology can cause a lot of harm for sure. ” Ohanian also said that building traditional social media apps is “not cool anymore”, as much of the web has been compromised, leaving him searching for what comes next for user-generated content (UGC).Ohanian now leads the venture capital firm Seven Seven Six, which manages over $1.3 billion in assets. Lately, he has turned his attention to sports, an area where he still sees genuine, real-life communities thriving “in the age of AI slop” and a “manipulated” internet. He is an open proponent of the “Dead Internet Theory,” the idea that bots now generate a massive share of online content and activity. According to Ohanian, large language models have put this trend into overdrive, with AI agents rapidly outpacing real people.“The internet that I grew up on … that was really built for humans first; user interfaces and experiences are going to go away,” Ohanian said, explaining that the web is increasingly being built for AI agents rather than human users.The boom in generative AI has created a complicated reality for platforms like Reddit. On one hand, Reddit’s massive archive of human conversations has become a goldmine, leading to lucrative data-licensing deals with companies like Google and OpenAI to train their models. “Platforms like ours became very, very valuable to LLMs,” Ohanian noted.On the other hand, the technology is \ undercutting the business. Just last week, Reddit’s shares dropped 29% after the company warned that Google’s AI-powered search was eating into its referral traffic. Beyond the stock price, Ohanian worries that turning online discussions into a commercial product has ruined their authenticity, leaving them full of “bullshit.”“The internet has gotten so manipulated because it is so incredibly valuable to do so,” he said.To combat third-party data scraping and protect user engagement, Reddit recently announced it will require users to sign in. While Ohanian declined to say whether he supports that specific policy, he stressed that “there has to be provable humanity on the internet without being creepy.”
Article Summary: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian believes the internet as we know it is fundamentally broken. He believes artificial intelligence (AI) is both a symptom and a driver of the shift. Ohanian warned that while AI holds massive promise, “there is still a very real chance that this technology can cause a lot of harm for sure”

Article Title: As $2.5 billion transferred from Binance in single transaction; how it cost hackers just $15; the massive cryptocurrency theft’s ‘big shock’
Article Text:
Cryptocurrency theft

How a ‘$15 transaction’ that cleared the vault

It took hackers just $15 to unlock access to $2.5 billion, followed by a matter of seconds to move the entire sum, to pull off the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. That striking reality sits at the center of the historic cryptocurrency theft from Binance, where attackers leveraged an advanced Ethereum feature to siphon roughly 40% of their total haul in one single transaction. This incident was part of a broader, sophisticated cyberattack that drained an estimated $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance, according to Bloomberg. The FBI has tied the breach to North Korea.Binance disclosed that the breach began when an engineer fell for a fake job posting and downloaded malicious code, granting the hackers entry into internal systems. What followed was a high-level exploitation of Ethereum’s underlying mechanics that allowed the intruders to move billions even while the exchange scrambled to lock down its operations.The central target was Binance 14, an active hot wallet used by the platform to handle regular customer withdrawals. Connected directly to online services, the wallet held massive balances of Ether, stablecoins and dozens of alternative tokens. Having breached Binance’s signing infrastructure, the attackers secured a valid cryptographic signature from the Binance 14 wallet. At around 8:20 p.m. UTC on October 29, they broadcasted instructions to the Ethereum network, paying roughly $15 in standard network gas fees.That $15 transaction did not move any cryptocurrency. Instead, it registered authorisation for the hackers' own software to operate the wallet.The negligible cost highlights how public blockchains function: Ethereum processing fees reflect the computational effort needed to run a piece of code and overall network demand – not the monetary value of the tokens inside an account. Modifying access rights on an account holding billions costs the exact same as doing so on an account holding a few dollars.Approximately three and a half minutes later, the attackers triggered their software to execute a single, sweeping transfer worth roughly $2.5 billion.The fast drain was caused by EIP-7702, an Ethereum improvement proposal introduced on May 7, 2025, during the network’s Pectra upgrade.Available for about 18 months, EIP-7702 was designed to streamline the user experience by giving standard crypto wallets programmable capabilities, like bundling multiple separate operations into a single step or allowing third parties to cover transaction fees. In everyday terms, it acts like appointing a concierge authorised to handle multiple errands without requiring sign-off on every task.Security analysts point out that EIP-7702 did not open the door on its own; the hackers had already infiltrated Binance's systems and compromised its signing credentials. However, the feature allowed the attackers' code to step directly into Binance 14's shoes.By using EIP-7702's bundling capabilities, the hackers consolidated the withdrawal into a single transaction that cleared 167,464 Ether, over 60 other cryptocurrencies, including roughly $1.6 billion worth of Tether (USDT) – the combined haul totaled approximately $2.5 billion.
Article Summary: Hackers used advanced feature to siphon roughly 40% of total haul in one transaction. Incident was part of a broader, sophisticated cyberattack that drained an estimated $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance. FBI has tied the breach to North Korea.

Article Title: After reported cases of broken bones, brain damage and other injuries; US Consumer Product Safety Commission issues red alert; tells Lowe’s, Costco and Amazon to recall 3.6 million …
Article Text:
Pic courtesy: US Consumer Product Safety Commission website

What US CPSC 'red notice' says

Which ladder models are being recalled

The US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) has issued an alert notifying consumers across America that 3.6 million ladders are being recalled because they could unexpectedly retract due to faulty locks. According to reports, warning comes after a number of people sustained broken bones, brain damage and other injuries.US CPSC has published a recall notice warning consumers that approximately 3,662,000 (3.6 million) ladders made by Little Giant Ladder Systems were being recalled after the company received several reports of the ladders unexpectedly retracting, causing serious injuries to users. As per CPSC's warning to buyers: "Ladders can suddenly retract if the Rapid Locks are not fully engaged, posing a fall hazard to consumers. "The faulty ladders have been sold on Lowes, Amazon, Costco, LittleGiantLadders and other websites. As per the consumer body, the 3.6 million-plus ladders included in this recall were sold nationally between December 2015 and October 2026. The ladders sold are priced anywhere from around $100 to around $1,000.The CPSC's notice says that the Rapid Locks are black or orange components on the ladders’ legs, designed to be inserted to adjust the ladders’ height.When the Rapid Locks don’t work as intended, the ladders can suddenly retract, causing the user to fall and sustain serious injuries. Little Giant has also published its own recall notice, in which the ladder manufacturer warns of the same hazard."Consumers should stop using the recalled ladders immediately until they review the information at http://www.littlegiantladders.com/pages/recalls or via the QR code on the ladder and contact Little Giant for a repair kit containing warning labels and instructions. The additional instructions and labels, which should be affixed to the ladder, advise consumers to verify that their Rapid Locks are properly engaged before every use and to maintain their locks with lubrication. Consumers who follow the provided instructions and have a Rapid Lock that does not function properly after the application of lubrication should contact Little Giant for evaluation. If a lock does not function properly after this evaluation, the company will offer the choice of a replacement ladder of the same or equivalent model or a refund ranging from a depreciated value determined by date of purchase up to full purchase price for ladders purchased within the past 12 months," said the USCPC on its page.The CPSC says the following models of Little Giant ladders are being recalled: Adjustable Fortress 2.0, Conquest 2.0, Dark Horse 2.0, Epic, King Kombo XT, Leveler, MegaLite, MegaLite+, Multi, Quantum and Vector.
Article Summary: US CPSC has published a recall notice warning consumers that approximately 3,662,000 (3.6 million) ladders made by Little Giant Ladder Systems were being recalled. The company received several reports of the ladders unexpectedly retracting, causing serious injuries to users. According to reports, people sustained broken bones, brain damage and other injuries.

“Ask Maps to help you get into town, find a great first meal, and discover what's happening tonight.”

“I just landed in %1$s! Help me get into town, recommend a great spot for my first meal, and tell me about what's happening tonight.”

How will Google Maps detect an arrival

An Android Authority report claims to have discovered signs of an airport-arrival notification system in version 26.45.00.1011720968 of the Android app. The feature appears designed to direct arriving passengers towards Ask Maps, its conversational AI tool, for help getting into a city, finding somewhere to eat and exploring local events.For users, this could provide a starting point for planning their first few hours after arrival. Instead of beginning with separate searches, travellers would receive a prompt to ask for suggestions together. Ask Maps lets users describe the places or activities they are looking for in ordinary language, rather than relying only on search filters.The notification title found in the code readswith the placeholder intended for the destination name. Its accompanying message says:The report also found a prepared request for Ask Maps:The report identified a background component called `AirportGeofenceSyncWorker`. Its presence suggests the feature would use location-based boundaries around airports to help detect arrivals.The precise conditions for triggering a notification remain unclear. The code findings do not establish how the app would distinguish a passenger arriving on a flight from someone visiting an airport for another reason.The report also raised the possibility that travel information from emails and calendar entries could provide additional context through Gemini Personal Intelligence, where enabled. That remains a possibility discussed in the report, rather than a confirmed part of the airport notification system.The findings reference more than 90 airport locations. Indian cities listed include Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad and Kolkata. Other locations include London, New York, Dubai, Singapore, Tokyo and Sydney.

When connected to a 350kW DC fast charger, it can add 200 miles of range in just 13 minutes.ID@undefined Caption not available.Built on Jaguar's new Electric Architecture (JEA), the Type 01 has been designed to offer a balance of performance and comfort. Its design includes a low roof, a long bonnet, a short front overhang and large 23-inch wheels. The car also has a 50:50 weight distribution, which is aimed at improving handling.Jaguar has also added intelligent torque vectoring and active aerodynamics to improve performance. These features include movable air vents and a rear spoiler that can extend in three stages. The car has a drag coefficient of 0.23, helping it move through the air more efficiently.The Type 01 has a cabin designed around luxury and technology. A central section divides the interior into four separate areas.The cabin features brass-effect aluminium trim, a 24-inch OLED driver display made from a single piece of glass and a separate 7-inch touchscreen. It also gets a full-width panoramic soundbar and seats with audio features designed to improve the listening experience.Jaguar says the name Type 01 reflects both its history and its future. The word "Type" pays tribute to famous models from the brand's past. The number "0" represents zero emissions, while "1" marks the first car of its new generation.The car also benefits from technology developed through Jaguar TCS Racing's Formula E programme, which has won two world championships.The Type 01 can accelerate from 62 mph to 112 mph (100km/h to 180km/h) in just 4.0 seconds.Designed, engineered and manufactured in the UK, the Type 01 is an important part of Jaguar's move towards becoming a fully electric luxury car brand. Prices start at £130,000, with the US price listed at $130,500. Higher-specification versions and customised models are expected to cost more than £150,000.Jaguar plans to open order books in early 2027, with the first customer deliveries expected in the second half of the year.Also read: Sebastien Buemi ends full-time Formula E career, stays with Envision as advisor
Article Summary: The Type 01 is Jaguar's new flagship electric car. It has three electric motors that produce 1,030PS of power and 1,365Nm of torque. It can go from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.2 seconds. Prices start at £130,000, with the US price listed at $130,500.

Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.
